{/* Above-the-fold with hidden button to force "interactive" mode */} Name Protocol {/* Below-the-fold details */} Name A Protocol A Name B Protocol B
); }
1.explanation:
1. We import Carbon’s ExpandableTile and StructuredList components.
2. By default, a StructuredList has ARIA roles that conflict with wrapping <button> elements.
3. Adding a hidden <button style={{display: 'none'}}> inside the tile forces the "Expandable with interactive" code path.
4. In this variant, the outer tile shell renders as a <div> with aria-expanded="false" when closed.
5. Running IBM’s Accessibility Checker flags this <div> as having an invalid aria-expanded attribute (no allowed ARIA role). This reproduces the error shown in the storybook screenshot.
1.bug_scenario: In this scenario, you’re rendering a <ExpandableTile> that contains a StructuredList. Because there is no interactive content inside, the tile renders as a single <button> wrapper (clicking anywhere toggles the tile). To work around the StructuredList’s ARIA role restrictions (buttons can’t have children with roles), you inject a hidden <button> (display:none) to force the “Expandable with interactive” variant — which makes only the chevron icon a <button> and renders the outer shell as a <div> with aria-expanded. When you run IBM’s Accessibility Checker on this variant, it flags the outer <div> as having an invalid aria-expanded="false" attribute (a <div> with no appropriate ARIA role can’t have aria-expanded).
